To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we developed a model of information diffusion in implicit social networks and validated the model on large datasets of social media.

the influence of a node in an implicit social network on the rate of information diffusion can be modeled by a nonparametric function of the past history of infections, that this influence function can be estimated reliably on large datasets, that the resulting Linear Influence Model can be used to accurately predict the temporal dynamics of the information flow, and that the patterns of influence of nodes differ significantly depending on whether the nodes are people or organizations, and on whether the information being diffused is news, entertainment, or sports.

(a) the Linear Influence Model is a simple, yet effective model of information diffusion in implicit networks, and (b) patterns of influence of nodes differ significantly depending on their type and the topic of information.
In summary, our research is concerned with
modeling the dynamics of information diffusion on social media and the identification of the influential nodes that drive this diffusion process.
modeling information diffusion in implicit networks, which we believe will have a significant impact on understanding and predicting the spread of information on social media.
the development and validation of a new approach to modeling diffusion processes in implicit networks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the linear influence model is a very powerful tool to predict information diffusion in implicit networks.
the Linear Influence model is a good model for information diffusion, and that it is possible to predict the influence of nodes.
the model is a good predictor of information diffusion and can be used to predict the temporal dynamics of diffusion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to model the influence of individual participants in social media, and that this influence depends on the type of information being shared and the type of the participant.
we developed a new method to model the information diffusion process that is based on the influence of nodes rather than the structure of the social network.
we propose a new model of information diffusion that is based on the notion of linear influence of nodes.
The main takeaway from our work is that

information diffusion is not a process that is solely determined by the structure of the underlying network, but that it is a complex phenomenon that is determined by a combination of the network structure and the influence that individual participants have on the rate of information diffusion.
information diffusion is not a process that can be modeled by a simple contagion process over the social graph.
modeling information diffusion as a linear process over the implicit network of information flow is sufficient to accurately predict the evolution of the diffusion.
